Answer: D
Reason: The CT scan (Figure 2) demonstrates an ill-defined, peripheral parenchymal consolidation in the left lower lobe with visible air bronchograms, a classic radiological appearance for Bronchiolitis Obliterans Organizing Pneumonia (BOOP), also known as Cryptogenic Organizing Pneumonia (COP). This diagnosis is strongly supported by the clinical history of persistent infiltrates that have failed to resolve with antibiotic treatment.
